Reach for `useLayoutEffect` when you need to measure or change the DOM and have that applied before the browser paints, for example measuring a tooltip's size and then positioning it, so users never see one frame of the wrong layout. `useEffect` runs after paint, which is right for almost everything else (fetching, subscriptions, logging). One catch: it doesn't run on the server, so in SSR code like Next you'll get a warning unless the measuring is client-only.
Action: Answer only, no code changes.

Most common cause is the form being submitted twice: htmx fires the `hx-post`, and the browser's normal submit also fires (or `hx-boost` and `hx-post` are both active), or the form was swapped in twice so there are two listeners. A quick guard is `hx-sync="this:drop"` plus `hx-disabled-elt` on the submit button, but I'd rather find the real double trigger first. I haven't seen the template yet, so I don't want to guess which one it is.
Action: Look at the add-hike form template and its `hx-*` attributes (and open the Network tab check: one POST or two?), then apply the fix.

A moved partial is a classic way to lose the token. Likely causes: the partial's `<form>` no longer has `{% csrf_token %}` inside it, the partial is rendered without the request (so the token comes out empty), or an `hx-headers` carrying `X-CSRFToken` was on an element that no longer wraps the form. I'd check in the Network tab whether the POST carries `X-CSRFToken` or a `csrfmiddlewaretoken` field at all.
Action: Ask you to paste the partial and the view that renders it (or look at them in trailmix), and I'll pinpoint which of those it is.

Middleware runs before every matched request, so Next made it run on the lightweight Edge runtime for fast startup and low latency close to the user, which is why it has a restricted API (no `fs`, limited Node modules). That's the limiting part. Newer Next versions can let middleware run on the Node.js runtime, but whether that's available depends on our Next version, so I'd check before promising it.
Action: Answer only; I can check the Next version in apps/web/package.json if you want to know whether Node runtime is an option.

AsyncLocalStorage lets you carry request-scoped context (request id, user, org) through async call chains without passing it as a parameter everywhere. The overhead is small for typical request context; I wouldn't worry unless it's on a very hot path, and I'd measure before deciding. It would also close the gap you hit with request ids, since the logger and the Sentry tagging could read the id from the store.

tsx transpiles TypeScript on the fly with esbuild, so it's fast and handles ESM and CJS together without extra config, but it does no type checking. ts-node uses the TypeScript compiler (type-checks unless you set transpile-only) and ESM needs loader setup. So with tsx you keep running `tsc` or typecheck separately. Also, I edited package.json by hand for tsx and haven't run an install, so the lockfile is still out of date.

The flicker comes from replacing the whole table, so the browser drops and rebuilds everything. The least dumb fix is the idiomorph extension: load it, set `hx-ext="morph"` and `hx-swap="morph:outerHTML"`, so only changed rows update. A cheaper alternative is to target just the `<tbody>` and swap its innerHTML, and give rows stable ids.
Action: Answer only; point me at the trail list template and I'll apply whichever you prefer.

A crash right after install with no output on a work laptop is most likely an old Node: the CLI has been ESM-only since PR #702, so older Node gives ERR_REQUIRE_ESM, though that isn't confirmed without their output. The reply would ask them to run `node -v`, upgrade to Node 18+, reinstall with `npm i -g @acme/cli`, and send the full error if it persists. A startup check written inside the ESM bundle can't run on a Node too old to load it, so the warning needs to live in a tiny entry that old Node can still execute (and an `engines` field would help, which was suggested but never added).
Action: Draft the support reply, then look at the CLI's bin entry and package.json to add the colored version warning and the engines field.
